title: STAT 579: Applied Causal Inference
text:
Course Overview
This graduate seminar offers a practical and intuitive journey into modern causal inference methods. We will explore how to move beyond simple correlation to identify and estimate causal effects from both experimental and observational data, with a focus on applications in public health, epidemiology, and clinical research.
The course emphasizes the practical application of methods and the critical assessment of causal claims in scientific literature. A central component of the seminar is a semester-long research project where you will ask and answer a causal question using real-world data.

Key Topics You Will Master:

The Potential Outcomes Framework
Causal Graphs (DAGs) and Graphical Identification (Backdoor, Frontdoor, do-calculus)
Matching and Propensity Score Methods
Instrumental Variables (IV)
Regression Discontinuity Designs (RDD)
Difference-in-Differences (DiD) and Panel Data Methods
Causal Mediation Analysis



Learning Objectives
Upon successful completion of this course, you will be able to: 1. Formulate a precise causal question from a substantive research problem. 2. Select, justify, and implement an appropriate causal inference method to address that question. 3. Critically evaluate the causal claims made in public health and biomedical literature.
